meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_2F_2306). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: TIER RE-PLACEMENT CANDIDATE: q23 tagged circle_theorem_tangent, which data/courses.ts lists as HIGHER-ONLY. It is on a FOUNDATION paper, and the specification backs the paper: Foundation 4.6 B is 'understand chord and tangent properties of circles', with the notes spelling out that tangents are perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact and that two tangents from a point are equal in length. The Higher listing adds the angle properties (4.6 C) and intersecting chords (4.6 A), not the tangent. Only one sighting so far, so this is recorded rather than acted on — see the final tally in docs/audit/25-igcse-4ma1-delta.md.

q9 tagged constructions: an accurate scale drawing of a triangle from two sides and the included angle, using ruler and protractor. The grid-based 'drawing' nodes do not cover a construction to given measurements.

q6(b) tagged measuring_lines_and_angles — FIRST sighting. The skill had read as unexamined across sixteen papers only because every earlier angle question sat on the lower node; here measuring a line with a ruler IS the mark.
q4 tagged sequences throughout: a stick-pattern sequence, drawn, tabulated, extended and then argued about. finding_the_nth_term would over-claim — the mark scheme accepts continuing the pattern.
q15(a),(b) tagged indices: both are about order of operations around a power, which has no node of its own and sits inside that skill's territory.
q14 and q16 tagged proportion for currency conversion and for a scale drawing, following the precedents in docs/coding-a-paper.md.
